subject: Mutual action playbook: acceptance tests, timeline & go-to-close cadence
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@brightwell.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Mutual action playbook: acceptance tests, timeline & go-to-close cadence

Elena — attaching our initial mutual action playbook (MAP) for the evaluation. I focused this version on concrete acceptance tests and the recommended timeline to hit a production decision in 2 weeks. Highlights:

- Evaluation window: 7 business days (short smoke + 5-day functional run).
- Exit gates: security review complete, P95 latency <= 250ms, inference cost within agreed target, functional pass-rate >= 95% on clinical-safety prompt set.
- Acceptance tests: smoke, throughput/canary, failover verification, datastore retention check, and data deletion verification.

Please review the attached MAP_Brightwell_v1.xlsx — tab 2 lists the acceptance-test steps I propose. If this lines up with Brightwell's expectations we'll lock dates and I can loop in Solutions for a focused runbook.

Attachments: MAP_Brightwell_v1.xlsx (xlsx, 12 KB)

Thanks,
--

Subject: Re: Mutual action playbook: acceptance tests, timeline & go-to-close cadence

Priyom — quick internal note before we send a final: can we tighten the functional pass-rate check to include a small stratified sample for false-positive/false-negative on clinical labels? Recommend adding:

- Acceptance Test 2b: Concordance sampling (n=500) stratified by diagnosis class; target F1 >= 0.88.
- Add canary rollback threshold: if observed P95 > 300ms for 3 consecutive 5-min windows, automated fallback to smaller model variant.

Also flag: SOC2 evidence may be requested by procurement — attaching a short SOC2 blurb we can hand off. I'll let Marissa confirm the SLA wording.

Karthik

From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@brightwell.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: Mark Turner <m.turner@brightwell.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Jul 2025 08:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Mutual action playbook: acceptance tests, timeline & go-to-close cadence

Thanks, Priyom. The MAP is a good start. A few clarifying questions before we lock the run dates:

1) Latency: we typically measure P95 at the application boundary (including network). Is your P95 target measured at the inference node or end-to-end? We need the latter.
2) Data: during the eval we will send PHI-like payloads (de-identified) — we need explicit confirmation on retention/deletion and KMS usage.
3) Duration: given our compliance reviews, can we extend the functional run to 7 days instead of 5? We want a slightly longer sample for throughput.

Procurement (Mark) — when we move to procurement, what evidence do you need to validate SOC2/attestation and what timing constraints should we expect for redlines?

Elena
Clinical Ops | Brightwell Health
elena.morales@brightwell.ai
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@brightwell.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jul 2025 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Mutual action playbook: acceptance tests, timeline & go-to-close cadence

Elena — great questions. Short answers up front, details below.

- Latency: we will provide end-to-end P95 numbers measured from your app logs + our standard tracing hook. For the MAP we will run both node-level and end-to-end measurements and report both; gate remains on end-to-end P95 <= 250ms.
- Data & retention: Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS for the eval. We will enable a 7-day retention window for KV/temporary caching during the run and execute an agreed deletion workflow at the end (we'll provide a deletion runbook and confirmation artifact).
- Duration: we are fine with extending functional run to 7 days. Proposed timeline below.

Proposed updated acceptance tests (short form):
- Smoke (30m): basic generation sanity, schema conformance.
- Canary (2 hours): ramp to 50 rps across two regions; P95 end-to-end < 250ms.
- Functional run (7 days): concordance sampling n=500 per day (stratified), F1 >= 0.88, pass rate >= 95% for safety prompts.
- Failover & recovery: simulate region failover, successful traffic shift within <90s and no data loss.
- Security & compliance: SOC2 summary (attached), KMS key rotation verification, retention/deletion verification step.

Attachments: eval_acceptance_tests.md (md, 9 KB); redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (pdf, 220 KB)

If that reads OK I'll lock the run Monday 21 Jul (start) through Monday 28 Jul (end) and open a shared Drive folder for run artifacts. I'll also ping Solutions to prep the test harness.

Thanks — Priyom
--
Priyom Das | Sr. Account Executive
Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0124

Subject: procurement: SOC2 evidence and timing for contract redlines

Priyom/Elena — procurement here. We appreciate the SOC2 summary. For contracting we will need:

- A copy of the SOC2 Type II report or an attestation letter and remediation notes for any exceptions.
- Standard data processing addendum (DPA) with KMS and deletion workflow clauses.
- Proposed commercial terms (SOW/quote) and a redline window of 7 business days.

Can you confirm you can provide the SOC2 report or an attestation by EOD Wed 23 Jul? Also please share a preliminary quote via DocuSign so we can get procurement review started.

Mark Turner
